headings: Use a method on your project
Adapt all three methods from one profile
rows.text:
Qore Skills

Prepare a sourced change plan, challenge a specification with independently checked findings, or inspect what a web interface actually does.

Qore is for developers and maintainers already using Codex on an existing project. It packages three independent methods as local skills. Choose the one your task needs; they are not a mandatory pipeline. No Qore account, backend, or hosted service is required.

Created by Sylvestre Franceschi at Qaizen. View the demonstration and diagrams.

In one actual self-application, planning exposed a malformed verifier option that produced a structural success token. The selected correction rejects it and keeps the earlier zero-finding review visible. See the problem, evidence, decision and limits.

Version 0.2.1. Three methods, a deterministic assembler, sourced profiles and recorded executions are included. The qualification record distinguishes original snapshots, corrective checks and coverage limits, including one explicit historical cache exclusion. Historical artifacts retain their original release state and identities.

Choose your task

$qore-plan prepares a change, $qore-review challenges an artifact, and $qore-ux-review observes a web flow.

You want to…	Target	Skill	Result	Prerequisites
Prepare or strengthen a change	Requirements or an existing specification	$qore-plan	Sourced specification, acceptance scenarios, adjudicated decisions, and task dependencies	Current project sources; five independent perspectives, scheduled in waves if needed
Challenge an artifact	Plan, specification, architecture document, or deliverable	$qore-review	Evidence-linked findings, retained refutations, and explicit verification gaps	Three independent finders and a fresh verifier; no browser required
Inspect rendered behavior	An authorized web entry, page, or flow	$qore-ux-review	Observed gate results, screenshots, defects, freshness, and scope limits	A working browser driver and the capabilities required by the declared scope

For an ordinary Git diff, prefer the host's available code-review workflow. Small tasks may need only clear repository instructions or a direct check. Qore adds a bounded protocol and evidence records when those are useful; no general quality, speed, or cost advantage is claimed.

Try one review

The first useful result is an actual review of the bundled validator-hardening specification, using its implementation and regression tests. This is a snapshot of Qore's own work, not a seeded defect. A valid zero-finding review is a possible result.

You need Codex with a local executor and independent subagent capability, plus python3, node, and Bash. The helpers use Python's standard library and Node built-ins. A browser, persistent project profile, and Qore account are unnecessary for this example. Merely loading a skill or passing a preflight does not complete the review.

Clone the public repository to use the current source. Git is needed for cloning; an existing checkout can skip it. Versioned archives are available from the releases page.

git clone https://github.com/sylvestre-baker/qore-codex-skills.git
cd qore-codex-skills


From the repository directory containing this README, build a new candidate and install its three skills into this checkout:

qore_stage="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/qore-first.XXXXXX")"
python3 tools/qore.py build --output "$qore_stage"
python3 tools/qore.py install --source "$qore_stage/qore-skills-0.2.1" --project-root .


The installer prints three paths under .agents/skills/ and "replaced": false. It refuses an existing destination and preserves it. If you already have these local skills, use a fresh checkout or compare a newly staged candidate; see safe updates.

For installation without the tutorial and evidence archive, the assembler also supports build --scope skills; see the compact archive guide. Download the compact skills ZIP for installation or the full ZIP for the tutorial, sources and evidence. Check their SHA-256 digests against the release assets. The explicit rights inventory covers the selected resource bytes; changed resources require a new review.

Open a new Codex chat in this repository directory, then use:

Use $qore-review to review examples/validator-hardening.md against its bundled
validators and tests. Keep the target to this specification and implementation.
Run the three independent finders, mechanical redaction, and a fresh verifier.
Retain phase evidence and report findings and execution coverage. Do not edit source files.


A completed example names the target snapshot, three returned finder reports, the actual redaction, a separate verifier, the final findings gate, and evidence for each phase. The report distinguishes COMPLETE / PARTIAL / BLOCKED execution coverage from finding impact and any delivery decision. Missing independence or an unfinished phase means PARTIAL or BLOCKED, even if the JSON is valid. Troubleshoot discovery or missing capabilities.

Use a method on your project

Install the verified candidate into your project's .agents/skills/ with the same installer and your project root as --project-root. Generic use reads the current sources you provide; it does not create a persistent profile.

Method	Starting prompt
Plan	Use $qore-plan to prepare this change from the current requirements and project sources. Preserve open decisions and show acceptance coverage.
Review	Use $qore-review to challenge docs/specs/change.md against its requirements and implementation. Report actual independent phases and uncovered scope.
Web UX	Use $qore-ux-review to inspect the authorized web flow from its real entry control. Declare required states and capabilities before execution; retain gaps and fresh evidence.

Supply the actual target, relevant requirements, and authorized web origin when applicable. A method can continue useful work while exposing unavailable sources, tools, data, or roles. It cannot label unobserved checks as passing. Fixes run only within the user's authorized scope; a profile or SHIP result does not grant merge, publication, or deployment permission.

See the evidence

The Qaizen Labs case shows all three specialized methods acting on one sourced profile. Planning separated Back keyboard reachability, resolved state and focus. Independent review reproduced four distinct coordination helper defects and retained separate post-fix verification. The actual desktop UX run followed the real entry, operated help and returned to the introduction without answering a question.

Watch the 105-second technical demonstration · Accessible English transcript · English captions · Static showcase preparation. The montage combines separate actual executions. The technical demonstration is separate from a personal application video.

The planning report, review and corrections, dated UX observations and actual PM acceptance connect the problem to a supported decision and explicit limits. The keyboard coverage gap was already known and concerned the protocol; it was not a newly discovered website bug.

Browser evidence covers one desktop English entry/state flow. It does not establish whole-site readiness, instrumented accessibility conformance, performance or external human usability. One analytics POST was blocked and recorded. Linux source review ran without a browser driver; its skipped browser checks are not passes. The earlier validator case and 0.1.0 execution record retain their original identities.

Evaluate a project adaptation

The Labs case shows the three specialized methods using project facts. It does not establish that specialization improves their results. The optional specialization evaluation asks a narrower question: for the tested obligations, should a maintainer retain, simplify or fix an adaptation?

All 18 original cells executed, including the retained pilot; 14 COMPLETE and 4 PARTIAL after independent coverage qualification. Comparative benefit remains UNKNOWN. Six related scenarios compare the same public source material under an agent baseline, generic Qore and derived Qore. Generic versus derived is the primary comparison; the baseline also changes the method and organization of work. Reconstructed tutorial protocols are labelled fixtures, not new website defects. Browser observations used the declared relay; failed requests and missing required checks remain visible. The campaign found a sourced-profile mismatch and a separately reproduced cookie-banner obstruction. Corrections have their own checks and do not replace the original trials.

Read the protocol and prerequisites, scenario registry, series registry and result inventory. This path is separate from the published review quickstart above. Preparation and structural checks do not count as completed agent trials.

Adapt all three methods from one profile

The methods stay reusable; a profile supplies the rules for one project. In the Labs example, a keyboard requirement changes the plan's acceptance checks, the review's evidence requirements and the browser actions.

flowchart LR
    Core["Three base skills: plan, review, UX review"] --> Assemble["Local assembler"]
    Profile["One sourced Labs profile: commands, rules, web entry"] --> Assemble
    Assemble --> Plan["qore-plan-qaizen-labs"]
    Assemble --> Review["qore-review-qaizen-labs"]
    Assemble --> UX["qore-ux-review-qaizen-labs"]


Diagram in words: three base methods plus one sourced project profile produce three specialized skills. Each contains its method, resources and copied profile. Codex loads the selected skill when you use it; the three methods can run independently.

Version 0.2.0 adds the Qaizen Labs project case: a public journey contract, one maintained profile and a keyboard verification correction. All three specialized methods have actual phase evidence; the final candidate documentation and release checks remain separately recorded. The optional PM/production workflow uses a private register and criteria-bound completion; its transport limitations remain explicit.

A reusable project adaptation binds the methods to sourced commands, invariants, and a web target. Every fact names a project source and its SHA-256. The included Qore profile applies to this repository; the contrasting fixture profile exercises isolation and different facts.

From this repository, generate three new project-specific skills:

python3 tools/qore.py derive --profile profiles/qore.json --project-root . --output /tmp/qore-derived-first
python3 tools/qore.py verify /tmp/qore-derived-first


Choose an unused output path. Derivation refuses stale sources or an existing destination. The generated names are qore-plan-qore, qore-review-qore, and qore-ux-review-qore. Each contains its own profile, references, and helper scripts. At invocation, its checker compares the target sources again and exposes only current applicable facts. Stale context makes affected coverage PARTIAL or BLOCKED; it never silently falls back to generic behavior.

For your project, maintain one profile from your actual rules and sources, then derive into new staging. Inspect the result and its diff before installing. Profile fields, runtime checks, and safe updates.

Optional: coordinate two terminals and a fresh reviewer

Terminal 1 tracks the task as PM. Terminal 2 produces the deliverable. The operator starts a separate reviewer session for the frozen delivery; Agent Mail carries their messages.

sequenceDiagram
    participant PM as Terminal 1: PM
    participant Prod as Terminal 2: Production
    participant Rev as Separate reviewer session
    Note over PM,Rev: The operator starts or resumes each work turn
    PM->>Prod: Assignment and acceptance criteria
    Prod->>PM: Explicit task acceptance
    Prod->>PM: Delivery, files and evidence
    PM->>Rev: Fresh review request, frozen delivery and criteria
    Rev->>PM: Verdict and proof
    PM->>PM: Check current identities, files and required proof
    alt Acceptance checks pass
        PM->>PM: Record DONE once
    else Corrections required
        PM->>Prod: Request correction, then a new delivery and review
    end


Diagram in words: PM assigns → production accepts and delivers → a separate session reviews → PM checks acceptance. Missing evidence keeps the task open. A rejected delivery needs correction and a new review. The local gate checks matching identities and proof files; substantive review remains a separate responsibility. The actual exchange records one accepted Labs delivery and the workflow's limits. All three skills also work without Agent Mail.

Understand the boundaries
Boundary	What the result means
Codex host	Actual role/tool availability must be observed. Five planning labels or a verifier flag do not prove independent execution. Clean candidate-only qualification is tracked separately.
Planning	Five perspectives, challenge, and adjudication; at most three rounds. Structural spec validation does not establish business completeness.
Review	Findings need checkable evidence. Only independently CONFIRMED critical/high findings are verified blockers. A critical/high PLAUSIBLE concern keeps its severity and requires PARTIAL/PENDING, even when the verifier ran. A separate confirmed blocker still requires DO-NOT-SHIP.
Web UX	Required checks need actual fresh browser evidence. Skipped required gates prevent global SHIP; six iterations is the ceiling, including persistent defects.
Native apps and other hosts	Unqualified by this web/Codex candidate. A web observation does not establish native behavior.
Validation	Digests and schemas check identity and structure. They do not prove reasoning quality, defect absence, or superiority over simpler workflows.
Human first use	No external human first-use outcome is claimed. Agent, maintainer, portability, and human observations remain separate.

Four complete method executions and two focused derivative probe suites are recorded with their own identities, plus structural regressions and post-correction checks. These are scope-specific execution checks, not a comparative benchmark. See qualification evidence and the independent Linux procedure for actual scope, isolation and credential boundaries.

Troubleshoot and update

An existing destination is preserved: build or derive into a new staging path, run the read-only comparison, and inspect changes before choosing any migration. A stale profile requires reconciling its source and regenerating; no silent generic fallback is permitted. Safe updates and observed failures and recovery cover these cases.

If a role or required browser capability is unavailable, retain its name and evidence gap. The result remains PARTIAL or BLOCKED; a flag, test total or clean console cannot replace the missing phase.

Reference and contribute
Releases, changelog, and publication record.
Architecture: core, project facts, Codex adaptation, and local trust boundaries.
Contracts and validators: project, release, and execution records; what checks can and cannot establish.
Command and prompt inventory: prerequisites, effects, substitutions, and actual execution status for the documentation examples.
Specialization evaluation: bounded scenarios, controlled inputs and evidence required before a comparative conclusion.
Troubleshooting: discovery, stale facts, unavailable tools, and refused updates.
Method protocols: planning, review, and web UX.
Contributing, provenance, and MIT license.
License and provenance

The newly authored implementation and documentation use the MIT license, maintained by Sylvestre Franceschi. The provenance record and explicit release rights inventory identify the scope of selected public observations and first-party resources. Private client distributions and their Git histories are excluded.

The public demonstration page presents the project-specific skills, agent coordination diagrams, narrated video and selected execution evidence. Its deployment uses an explicit workflow dispatch from main. Publication provenance separates hosted checks from historical method executions.

First-party repository content is maintained in English. External quotations, rendered evidence and protocol tokens retain their source identity. Publication and any external application remain separate actions.

headings: Browser observations use a declared operator relay
Read results without manufacturing a winner
rows.text:
Evaluate a project adaptation

All 18 original cells executed, including the retained pilot; 14 COMPLETE and 4 PARTIAL after independent coverage qualification. Comparative benefit remains UNKNOWN.

Use this optional protocol to decide whether to retain, simplify or fix an adaptation for the obligations tested on Qaizen Labs. For your first Qore result, use the published review quickstart. The recorded Labs case remains separate from this experiment.

What the comparison can establish

The primary comparison is generic Qore versus derived Qore. They receive the same task and may consult the same original project sources. The derived skill organizes those facts through the existing sourced profile. It receives no exclusive project information and the invocation does not repeat the expected rule.

Condition	Instructions and project context
Baseline	The task and original project sources, without Qore. This also changes the method and organization of work.
Generic	The same task and sources, with the selected generic method.
Derived	The same task and sources, with its generated Qaizen Labs derivative.

Each cell uses a fresh context. The candidate, source digests, model configuration, tools and declared budget identify the execution. A valid baseline need not perform Qore phases. Generic and derived reports retain their methods’ required phases and execution records.

One observation in each of eighteen cells is a bounded diagnostic. Six related scenarios on one project do not demonstrate general superiority, statistical reliability, cost savings or robustness to future models. Observed time and resource use are reported with their limits rather than converted into a productivity claim.

Six related scenarios

The scenario registry is the machine-readable authority for the inputs and criteria. The series registry accounts for the three conditions in every scenario, including cells not launched.

Scenario	Task	Expected evidence
P1	Plan correction of an incomplete protocol.	Separate criteria for keyboard traversal, returned state and focus, with source-backed checks.
P2	Plan a documentation clarification of a correct protocol.	Preserve valid obligations without inventing an application change.
R1	Review the incomplete protocol.	Identify missing evidence without claiming a proven website defect.
R2	Review its corrected comparator.	An empty review is valid; any additional finding needs support.
U1	Observe the actual Back journey from the public entry.	Keyboard traversal, return state, heading focus and unanswered state.
U2	Observe help opening and closing.	Closure, focus on the help summary and an unchanged unanswered question.

The protocol documents are reconstructed tutorial fixtures, newly authored for this evaluation. They are not historical public revisions or newly discovered website defects. The corrected comparator is unavailable to P1 and R1 workers. Synthetic controls qualify the protocol; they do not replace real browser observations.

The criteria examine relevant project rules, evidence, omissions, unsupported assertions, valid empty findings, unnecessary changes and justified decisions. Reading a profile is not proof of using it: the result must identify its effect on an action or conclusion.

Prepare the environment before trials

Observed recovery: the original no-model probe failed before command execution. A separately qualified disposable Linux runtime then ran the pilot and all remaining cells. It used an explicit scoped seccomp syscall allowance, UID 1000, dropped capabilities, no new privileges, no host mounts, a named inner filesystem sandbox, disabled connectors and observed parent/child boundary controls. Model transport remained available; command networking did not. This qualifies the recorded environment, not arbitrary Docker installations or the historical clean-room default.

Workers must not reach old answers, reports, evaluator keys, neighboring cell results, private sources, personal skill directories or the full repository history. A new chat alone does not establish that isolation. The common input bundle contains the selected sources and the target document; each Qore condition also receives its complete autonomous skill resources.

Before a cell starts, record actual model and tool availability, test the source boundary, and check that tools cannot reach alternate search or network paths. Keep model transport separate from tool-network permissions. Recheck input digests after the trial. A violated boundary invalidates comparability; an unavailable required capability leaves the cell incomplete or blocked. Do not substitute the author’s main conversation.

Use the declared budgets and order in the series. The first balanced R1 group checks capture, isolation and feasibility. Its outcome does not determine whether the experiment proceeds. A material protocol correction preserves the pilot separately and restarts the balanced series; only one pilot correction is permitted. This means at most twenty-one attempted cells, rather than silently replacing unfavorable results.

Browser observations use a declared operator relay

The agent requests a complete sequence of at most forty actions. An operator executes it in the existing observation harness and returns actual screenshots, DOM, events and diagnostics. The operator does not fix selectors, repair the route, suggest a missing check or continue the agent’s reasoning.

What the comparison can establish

The primary comparison is generic Qore versus derived Qore. They receive the same task and may consult the same original project sources. The derived skill organizes those facts through the existing sourced profile. It receives no exclusive project information and the invocation does not repeat the expected rule.

Condition	Instructions and project context
Baseline	The task and original project sources, without Qore. This also changes the method and organization of work.
Generic	The same task and sources, with the selected generic method.
Derived	The same task and sources, with its generated Qaizen Labs derivative.

Each cell uses a fresh context. The candidate, source digests, model configuration, tools and declared budget identify the execution. A valid baseline need not perform Qore phases. Generic and derived reports retain their methods’ required phases and execution records.

One observation in each of eighteen cells is a bounded diagnostic. Six related scenarios on one project do not demonstrate general superiority, statistical reliability, cost savings or robustness to future models. Observed time and resource use are reported with their limits rather than converted into a productivity claim.

Six related scenarios

The scenario registry is the machine-readable authority for the inputs and criteria. The series registry accounts for the three conditions in every scenario, including cells not launched.

P2	Plan a documentation clarification of a correct protocol.	Preserve valid obligations without inventing an application change.
R1	Review the incomplete protocol.	Identify missing evidence without claiming a proven website defect.
R2	Review its corrected comparator.	An empty review is valid; any additional finding needs support.
U1	Observe the actual Back journey from the public entry.	Keyboard traversal, return state, heading focus and unanswered state.
U2	Observe help opening and closing.	Closure, focus on the help summary and an unchanged unanswered question.

The protocol documents are reconstructed tutorial fixtures, newly authored for this evaluation. They are not historical public revisions or newly discovered website defects. The corrected comparator is unavailable to P1 and R1 workers. Synthetic controls qualify the protocol; they do not replace real browser observations.

The criteria examine relevant project rules, evidence, omissions, unsupported assertions, valid empty findings, unnecessary changes and justified decisions. Reading a profile is not proof of using it: the result must identify its effect on an action or conclusion.

The protocol, scenario registry, series registry and generated summary identify exact inputs and later coverage qualification. Recompute the summary using the documented helper. The earlier Labs case retains its separate original identity.

All original attempts
Scenario	Agent baseline	Qore generic	Qore derived
P1	COMPLETE	COMPLETE	COMPLETE
P2	COMPLETE	COMPLETE	COMPLETE
R1	COMPLETE	COMPLETE	COMPLETE
R2	COMPLETE	COMPLETE	COMPLETE
U1	COMPLETE	PARTIAL	PARTIAL
U2	COMPLETE	PARTIAL	PARTIAL

These are eighteen attempts in total, including the original balanced R1 pilot; none was excluded or rerun to improve its result. COMPLETE describes execution coverage, not correct recommendations or product readiness. Every original method declaration remains unchanged beside its later independent qualification. The protocol fixtures are labelled reconstructions, not historical website defects.

What the evidence supports
Fix the profile: the frozen Qaizen profile allowed Tab or Shift+Tab while its source selected forward Tab. Hash freshness alone did not establish semantic fidelity. Review outputs repeated the broader convention in some conditions. Profile 0.1.1 and all three derivative preflights now preserve the source-selected obligation. This supports a targeted correction, not a generic-versus-derived winner.
Fix an observed interface obstruction: a separate native viewport/geometry reproduction confirmed that the cookie banner could cover the focused Back control. The private website correction passed local desktop, narrow-width and resize checks plus independent verification. It remains a local commit, not a deployed production change. Selected correction evidence.
Fix the operator and reporting: the frozen harness advertised a text locator it did not resolve; later code and actual Chromium tests cover that locator and viewport capture. Original failed requests are preserved. Required missing deep-entry checks restrict coverage; an outer COMPLETE label cannot replace them. Later qualification can restrict coverage and cannot promote it.
Preserve refutations: allegations that mechanical redaction exposed entire finder reports were independently refuted. The exact allowlisted fields may still contain reasoning; filtering is not semantic blinding. The procedural separation and this limit are explicit.

Planning results supplied useful source-backed acceptance checks, while relevant review and browser results exposed both supported observations and uncertainty. All entered comparative decisions remain Unknown. The observations do not isolate a general benefit of specialization.

Qualification, evaluation and limits
Item	Observation
Runtime	Actual qualified recovery, scoped security change, parent/child controls, source-bound inputs, existing model transport. No author conversation substituted for workers.
Candidate identity	Frozen candidate SHA-256 8b26119f383a7d5853c1bd2ab5f678e08966300846c0d6f2784351c1f5a59e8d; corrected code has separate identities.
Independent evaluation	Separate planning, review and UX evaluators, then later independent verification; selected reports and evidence mapping. Neutral IDs did not blind conditions.
Coverage	Required missing observations and conflicts remain visible; original declarations, task-criterion judgments and qualified coverage are distinct.
Timing	Child wall intervals are conservative, exact aggregate compute unavailable; late role returns, missed expiry monitoring and one evaluator cap overrun retained.
Browser limits	Live deployment revision unverified; frozen screenshots were full-page, so historical viewport obstruction was not established by those images alone. The later native viewport reproduction has its own identity.
Portability	Observed disposable Linux arm64 runtime with the recorded CLI, host relay and tooling; not arbitrary-host certification.
Qodo review	NOT_OBSERVED, optional and separate.
External human first use	NOT_OBSERVED. Agent and maintainer checks are not human usability evidence.
Publication	Prepared on a draft PR; no new release, deployment, client migration, outreach or application submission.

Full model/CLI traces, credentials, private website source and browser videos/trace archives remain excluded. The provenance records map public selections to original digests and declared transformations. Exact historical worker reports retain original links; a narrowly hash-pinned exception requires a navigable maintained adapter and grants no runtime-path exemption. Two partial archived source copies have explicitly listed, byte-identical frozen input companions added for export closure; these are presentation resources, not evidence of worker consumption.

Actual correction regressions and local document rendering observations retain their scope and source identities.
